PH IS THIRD MOST CONGESTED COUNTRY IN THE WORLD AND THE MOST CONGESTED IN ASIA 

The Philippines was the third most congested country in the world with an average congestion level of 44.6% in 2025. Meanwhile, the Philippines was the most congested country in Asia.

Davao City and Manila were the most congested cities and metro areas in the Philippines in 2025. 

Among 492 cities, Davao City ranked 11th most congested among metro areas and 12th most congested among cities.  Manila ranked 14th most congested among metro areas and 40th among cities.

TRAFFIC SA PILIPINAS 🚦

Davao City ang tinaguriang most traffic-congested city sa Pilipinas, base sa 2025 TomTom Traffic Index.

Tinatayang nasa 4.4 kilometers ang layo ng nababiyahe sa lungsod sa loob ng 15 minuto. Nasa 168 oras din ang nasasayang sa rush hour dito kada taon.

Pagdating sa worldwide ranking, nasa 12th spot ang Davao City. Pang-40 naman sa listahan ang Manila.

Kinilala rin ang Pilipinas bilang most traffic-congested country sa Asya matapos maitala ang congestion rate na 45%.

Ibinabase ng TomTom ang kailang datos sa GPS data at real driving speeds.

FULL LIST: https://t.co/ToHHn0Z6Hu

Mas malakas at maigting na kolaborasyon ang naging sentro ng pulong sa pagitan ni Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) General Manager USec. Nicolas Torre III at ng mga opisyal mula University of the Philippines Resilience Institute (UPRI) at UP National Center for Transportation Studies (NCTS).

Tinalakay sa naging pulong ang traffic at flood control initiatives sa Metro Manila at ang mga pamamamaraan para magtulungan ang dalawang ahensiya. Kabilang sa mga napag-usapan ang pagtulong ng UPRI para makapag-develop ng app tulas ng Project NOAH na maaaring magamit kapag may kalamidad. Magkakaroon din ng data sharing ang UPRI at MMDA para sa mga flooded area sa NCR.

Mga seminar at training naman para sa mga personnel ng ahensiya ang pinag-usapan ni USec. Torre at ng mga opisyal ng NCTS. 

Kabilang sa pagpupulong sina UPRI Executive Director Mahar Lagmay, Prof. Ranjit Rye, NCTS Director Jun Castro, Engr. Shiela Flor Javier, VP Joel Marciano, at UP Office of the President Head Executive Assistant Karlo Miguel Abuda.

#mmda

SENATE ALMOST CAUGHT FIRE AGAIN

LOOK: A power bank exploded inside the Bills and Index Service office at the Senate building in Pasay around 3:50 p.m., sparking a small fire that was quickly put out with an extinguisher.

Fire personnel arrived at 4:05 p.m. and declared the incident under control, according to a report shared by Senate Secretary Rey Bantug.

A fire hit an office on the third floor of the Senate building on Nov. 30, damaging the session hall below. The affected area has been repaired. | @eimorpsantos
